arxiv-1811-02070.title: Blind Two-Dimensional Super-Resolution and Its Performance Guarantee (Extended Version)
arxiv-1811-02070.creator: Mohamed A. Suliman, Wei Dai
arxiv-1811-02070.description: Abstract We study the problem of identifying the parameters of a linear system from its response to multiple unknown waveforms. We assume that the system response is a scaled superposition of time-delayed and frequency-shifted versions of the unknown waveforms. Such kind of problem is severely ill-posed and does not yield a unique solution without introducing further constraints.

arxiv-2112-04570.creator: Oliver Nash
arxiv-2112-04570.description: Abstract . Lie algebras are an important class of algebras which arise throughout mathematics and physics. We report on the formalisation of Lie algebras in Lean’s Mathlib library. Although basic knowledge of Lie theory will benefit the reader, none is assumed; the intention is that the overall themes will be accessible even to readers unfamiliar with Lie theory.

arxiv-2301-12265.title: Hypercyclic operators on Hilbert C*-modules
arxiv-2301-12265.creator: Stefan Ivković
arxiv-2301-12265.description: Abstract . In this paper we characterize hypercyclic generalized bilateral weighted shift operators on the standard Hilbert module over the C ∗ C^{*} -algebra of compact operators on the separable Hilbert space. Moreover, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for these operators to be chaotic and we provide concrete examples. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 47A16 1.

arxiv-2307-08127.title: This article is part of an OCNMP Special Issue
arxiv-2307-08127.creator: in Memory of Professor Decio Levi
arxiv-2307-08127.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by in Memory of Professor Decio Levi. We study reductions of the Volterra lattice corresponding to stationary equations for the additional, noncommutative subalgebra of symmetries. It is shown that, in the case of general position, such a reduction is equivalent to the stationary equation for a sum of the scaling symmetry and the negative flows, and is written as ( m + 1 ) (m+1) -component difference equations of the Painlevé type generalizing the dP 1 and dP 34 equations.

arxiv-2309-07227.description: Abstract Pulsar timing arrays have found evidence for a low-frequency gravitational wave background (GWB). Assuming the GWB is produced by supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), the next gravitational wave (GW) signals astronomers anticipate are Continuous Waves (CWs) from single SMBHBs and their associated GWB anisotropy.

arxiv-2401-07112.creator: Gerardo Morales-Herrera, Pablo Ortega-Ruiz, Mehrab Momennia, Alfredo Herrera-Aguilar
arxiv-2401-07112.description: Abstract In this paper, we employ a general relativistic formalism and develop new theoretical tools that allow us to analytically express the mass and electric charge of the Reissner-Nordström black hole as well as its distance to a distant observer in terms of few directly observable quantities, such as the total frequency shift, aperture angle of the telescope, and redshift

arxiv-2403-00353.title: MS-Net: A Multi-Path Sparse Model for Motion Prediction in Multi-Scenes
arxiv-2403-00353.creator: Xiaqiang Tang, Weigao Sun, Siyuan Hu, Yiyang Sun, Yafeng Guo
arxiv-2403-00353.description: Abstract The multi-modality and stochastic characteristics of human behavior make motion prediction a highly challenging task, which is critical for autonomous driving. While deep learning approaches have demonstrated their great potential in this area, it still remains unsolved to establish a connection between multiple driving scenes (e.g., merging, roundabout, intersection) and the design of deep learning models.

arxiv-2407-02838.title: Designing Superionic Conductors Using Tetrahedrally Packed Structures
arxiv-2407-02838.creator: Tomoyasu Yokoyama, Kazuhide Ichikawa, Takuya Naruse, Kosei Ohura, Yukihiro Kaneko
arxiv-2407-02838.description: Abstract In the pursuit of advanced energy storage solutions, the crystal structure of ionic conductors plays a pivotal role in facilitating ion transport. The conventional structural design principle that compounds with the body-centered cubic (BCC) anionic frameworks have high ionic conductivity is well known.

arxiv-2503-19732.title: Grid-Free Evaluation of Phonon-Limited Electronic Relaxation Times and Transport Properties
arxiv-2503-19732.creator: Nenad Vukmirović
arxiv-2503-19732.description: Abstract Present calculations of electrical transport properties of materials require evaluations of electron-phonon coupling constants on dense predefined grids of electron and phonon momenta and performing the sums over these momenta. In this work, we present the methodology for calculation of carrier relaxation times and electrical transport properties without the use of a predefined grid.

arxiv-2506-04559.title: Perceptual Decoupling for Scalable Multi-modal Reasoning via Reward-Optimized Captioning
arxiv-2506-04559.creator: Yunhao Gou, Kai Chen, Zhili Liu, Lanqing Hong, Xin Jin, Zhenguo Li, James T. Kwok, Yu Zhang
arxiv-2506-04559.description: Abstract Recent advances in slow-thinking language models ( e.g. , OpenAI-o1 and DeepSeek-R1) have demonstrated remarkable abilities in complex reasoning tasks by emulating human-like reflective cognition. However, extending such capabilities to the multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) remains challenging due to the high cost of retraining vision-language alignments when upgrading the underlying reasoner LLMs.

arxiv-2506-21824.title: Symmetry analysis of cross-circular and parallel-circular Raman optical activity
arxiv-2506-21824.creator: Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Gakuto Kusuno, Takuya Satoh, Ryotaro Arita
arxiv-2506-21824.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Gakuto Kusuno, Takuya Satoh, Ryotaro Arita. The Raman scattering regarding the circularly-polarized incident and scattered lights is closely related to the circular activity of a given system. We investigate the symmetry of its activity, called the cross-circular and parallel-circular Raman optical activity. The analysis is systematically performed with the magnetic point groups and indicates that the response allows for a useful diagnosis of the symmetry of materials like chirality and (magneto-)axiality.

arxiv-2601-10451.title: Localization Landscape in Non-Hermitian and Floquet quantum systems
arxiv-2601-10451.creator: David Guéry-Odelin, François Impens
arxiv-2601-10451.description: Abstract We propose a generalization of the Filoche–Mayboroda localization landscape that extends the theory well beyond the static, elliptic and Hermitian settings while preserving its geometric interpretability. Using the positive operator H † ​ H H^{\dagger}H , we obtain a landscape that predicts localization across non-Hermitian, Floquet, and topological systems without computing eigenstates.

pmc-10620390.title: Quantification and characterization of biological activities of glansreginin A in black walnuts (Juglans nigra)
pmc-10620390.creator: Khanh-Van Ho, Hsien-Yeh Hsieh, Anuradha Roy, Sarah Foote, Peter McDonald, Mark V Coggeshall, Hideyuki Ito, Zhentian Lei, Lloyd W Sumner, George C Stewart, Chung-Ho Lin
pmc-10620390.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Glansreginin A has been reported to be an indicator of the quality of walnuts (Juglans spp.). However, bioactive properties of glansreginin A have not been adequately explored. In the present study, we quantified concentrations of glansreginin A in black walnuts (Juglans nigra) using high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC–MS/MS) and performed an array of in vitro bioassays to characterize biological activities (e.g., antibacterial, antioxidant, anticancer capacities) of this compound.

pmc-11445617.title: Probiotics in the management of radiation-induced oral mucositis
pmc-11445617.creator: Yixuan Li, Zixia Li, Shuhao Zheng, Xin Xu
pmc-11445617.description: Oral mucositis is a common and debilitating oral complication in head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy, resulting in diminished quality of life and potential treatment disruptions. Oral microbiota has long been recognized as a contributing factor in the initiation and progression of radiation-induced oral mucositis (RIOM).

pmc-11698161.title: Prevalence of central nervous system-active polypharmacy in a cohort of older adults in Argentina
pmc-11698161.creator: Augusto Ferraris, Federico Angriman, Tomas Barrera, Paula Penizzotto, Sol Faerman, Washington Rivadeneira, Alan Chiessa, Gaspar Mura, Javier Alberto Pollán, Alejandro G Szmulewicz
pmc-11698161.description: BackgroundCentral nervous system (CNS)-active polypharmacy is frequent and potentially harmful in older patients. pmc-12381336.title: The effect of stress on prospective memory in robotic command and control
pmc-12381336.creator: Mollie R. McGuire, Robert S. Gutzwiller
pmc-12381336.description: Remembering to carry out an intention at the appropriate time (prospective memory—PM) requires attentional resources that may be limited in stressful circumstances. PM failures in high-risk/high stress environments, such as military operations, can have fatal consequences, and yet, the effect of stress on PM has received little attention.

pmc-12571513.title: Severe Necrotizing Pneumonia Caused by Panton‑Valentine Leukocidin‑Producing Staphylococcus aureus in a Previously Healthy Adult
pmc-12571513.creator: Prabin Paudyal, Pallavi Bedi
pmc-12571513.description: A previously healthy adult male presented with rapidly progressive pneumonia and systemic features of infection shortly after returning from travel abroad. Despite broad‑spectrum antimicrobial therapy and supportive measures, he deteriorated into respiratory failure requiring ICU admission and mechanical ventilation. Imaging revealed cavitating lung nodules and necrosis. Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL)‑positive Staphylococcus aureus (PVL‑SA) was confirmed by PCR.

pmc-13104189.creator: Unknown
pmc-13104189.description: b performance. While burnout among healthcare providers has been studied, there is limited research on burnout in the Canadian public health workforce. Participants were public health workers involved in various roles during the pandemic aged 18 years and older.

pmc-13380132.title: Visual Outcomes and Patient Satisfaction With a New Trifocal, Toric Intraocular Lens
pmc-13380132.creator: Zachary Zavodni, Shweta Negi

PurposeDescribe visual outcomes, rotational stability, and patient experience with a new, trifocal, toric intraocular lens (IOL), CNWTTx (Alcon, Fort Worth, TX.)Patients and methodsProspective, cohort study in a private practice in Salt Lake City, UT. Patients 45 years and older with visually significant cataracts, bilateral regular corneal astigmatism requiring a T3‐T6 IOL power lens, no other significant eye disease undergoing sequential cataract surgery with Clareon PanOptix Toric IOL (CNWTTx) followed for 3 months postoperatively.

pmc-13414950.title: Spatial associations between esophageal lesions and surrounding tissues in esophageal fistula: a CAM-guided radiomics study
pmc-13414950.creator: Ang Li, Lili Lin, Zewen Han, Jianqiang Ye, Junqing Lin, Han Jiang
pmc-13414950.description: ObjectiveEsophageal fistula is a life-threatening complication following treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging due to the limited predictive value of conventional imaging markers. This study aimed to develop and validate a Grad-CAM–guided deep learning–radiomics framework for risk prediction and spatial biomarker discovery using pre-treatment CT.

pmc-13486016.title: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea and anti-Müllerian hormone: insights for fertility assessment
pmc-13486016.creator: Giovanna Notaristefano, Anna Tropea, Anastasiya Samasiuk, Monia Ranalli, Martina Asia Policriti, Alice Diterlizzi, Tullio Ghi, Antonio Lanzone, Rosanna Apa
pmc-13486016.description: BackgroundAnti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) is widely used as a marker of ovarian reserve. However, its reliability in functional hypothalamic amenorrhea (FHA) remains debated. FHA is characterized by reduced gonadotropin secretion and impaired folliculogenesis, which may influence AMH expression and lead to an underestimation of reproductive potential.MethodsWe conducted a case–control study including women diagnosed with FHA and age-matched healthy controls.

uslaw-usc-t31-s6203.title: 31 U.S.C. § 6203 — Printing and distribution of reports and machine-readable records
uslaw-usc-t31-s6203.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s6203.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 62 (Consolidated Federal Funds Report). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) (1) The Director shall— (A) prepare— (i) printed copies of each of the reports required by this chapter; and (ii) machine-readable records of such reports; and (B) make the printed copies of the reports and the machine-readable records available to the public.

uslaw-usc-t33-s5.title: 33 U.S.C. § 5 — Abolition of tolls on Government canals, canalized rivers, etc.; expense of operation, repairs to and reconstruction of canals, etc.; Panama Canal excepted; levies by non-Federal interest
uslaw-usc-t33-s5.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t33-s5.description: United States Code, Title 33 (Navigation And Navigable Waters); Chapter 1 (Navigable Waters Generally); Subchapter I (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) No tolls or operating charges whatever shall be levied upon or collected from any vessel, dredge, or other water craft for passing through any lock, canal, canalized river, or other work for the use and benefit of navigation.

uslaw-usc-t40-s6908.title: 40 U.S.C. § 6908 — Parking facility
uslaw-usc-t40-s6908.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t40-s6908.description: United States Code, Title 40 (Public Buildings, Property, And Works); Part C (Federal Building Complexes); Chapter 69 (Union Station Redevelopment); Subchapter I (Union Station Complex). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Title.— The Federal Government has the right, title, and interest in and to the parking facility at Union Station. (b) Fees.— The rate of fees charged for use of the facility.
